correctness.rationale: The exact conditional sign mean is \(m_n=(1-2p_n)^{\binom{S_n}{d}}\). Uniformly in the count of negative increments, it has an order-\(n^{-1}\) approximation by \(\exp[-2\lambda(S_n/n)^d/d!]\). Taylor expansion at one half gives \(m_n-\rho=aX_n/n+R_n\), with \(\|R_n\|_2=O(n^{-1})\) and aggregate remainder negligible on the square-root scale. The history sum has harmonic weights whose sum equals \(N\) and whose squared sum equals twice \(N\) minus the harmonic number. Multivariate Lindeberg gives history covariance entries one, one and two. Independent conditional coefficient-row errors have limiting normalized variance \(1-\rho^2\), and their Gaussian limit is independent of the increment history because conditional characteristic functions converge to a nonrandom limit. Orthogonality and the negligible remainder also prove the moments. The first-order quenched limit follows by Hoeffding, Fubini and a bounded martingale functional CLT. The bundled finite checker passes 824 assertions but is not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The investigated 2026 and 2020 primary sources characterize first-order joint Brownian convergence and in particular 2026 Proposition 10 includes an arbitrary row-independent coefficient grouping, so the first-order sparse correlation alone would be covered conceptually. The final claim instead computes a second-order annealed CLT and exact asymptotic variance/covariance of the empirical bracket, with a degree-identifiability phenomenon at equal Brownian correlation. The inspected source statements do not give this second-order law and targeted published-finding corpus searches and accessible prior claims found no direct coverage. A broader unlocated fluctuation theorem remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: A general martingale fluctuation/triangular-array theorem in prior literature might yield the same second-order Gaussian variance after specializing, although no directly covering statement was found.

value.rationale: Degree-restricted activation mechanisms can be calibrated to the same first-order Brownian correlation \(\rho\). Nevertheless the empirical cross-covariation has asymptotic variance \(1-\rho^2+2d^2\rho^2(\log\rho)^2\) and covariance with the original walk \(-d\rho\log\rho\). This separates invisible first-order mechanisms using a canonical second-order observable, quantitatively decomposing fresh-coefficient randomness and feedback from shared increment history; it is not merely a reparameterization of the first-order invariance principle.
